$about: The 78 cards for the Daily Oracle (1c). The card's identity and art sit outside `reading`; A. E. Waite's divinatory meanings sit inside it, quoted verbatim as printed, with their source, credit, and review flag, so a reviewed reading replaces `reading` card by card with no code change. The day shows the upright meaning only; the reversed stays in the data. `name` is the card's own title (Waite's list heads card 8 Fortitude and card 20 The Last Judgment; see nameInWaite). Alt texts are Claude's placeholders. Art: lib/tarot-files.json; where each image comes from: credits.json.

waite-pkt.short: A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot
waite-pkt.work: The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, being fragments of a secret tradition under the veil of divination
waite-pkt.author: Arthur Edward Waite
waite-pkt.firstEdition: 1911 (the title page; released in December 1910). The unillustrated Key to the Tarot is the 1910 book.
waite-pkt.transcribedFrom: the 1922 Rider reprint (title page 1922; its verso reads "First Published 1910, Reprinted 1922"), as transcribed on Wikisource: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Pictorial_Key_to_the_Tarot, page images at https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Pictorial_Key_to_the_Tarot.pdf
waite-pkt.checkedAgainst: https://archive.org/details/a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot (an OCR of the sacred-texts transcription of the first edition); every difference settled on the page image
waite-pkt.part: Part III: the Greater Arcana and their divinatory meanings (pp. 283 to 287), and the Lesser Arcana, one card to a page (pp. 170 to 280)

cards.name: The Fool
cards.alt: A young traveler in a bright tunic steps toward a cliff edge, a white rose in hand and a small white dog at his heels

reading.upright: Folly, mania, extravagance, intoxication, delirium, frenzy, bewrayment.
reading.reversed: Negligence, absence, distribution, carelessness, apathy, nullity, vanity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: The Magician
cards.alt: A robed figure raises a wand to the sky and points to the ground, a cup, a sword, and a pentacle on the table before him

reading.upright: Skill, diplomacy, address, subtlety; sickness, pain, loss, disaster, snares of enemies; self-confidence, will; the Querent, if male.
reading.reversed: Physician, Magus, mental disease, disgrace, disquiet.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.alt: A seated woman in blue robes holds a scroll between a black pillar and a white pillar, a crescent moon at her feet

reading.upright: Secrets, mystery, the future as yet unrevealed; the woman who interests the Querent, if male; the Querent herself, if female; silence, tenacity; mystery, wisdom, science.
reading.reversed: Passion, moral or physical ardour, conceit, surface knowledge.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The Empress
cards.alt: A crowned woman rests on cushions in a field of wheat, a heart-shaped shield beside her and a stream behind

reading.upright: Fruitfulness, action, initiative, length of days; the unknown, clandestine; also difficulty, doubt, ignorance.
reading.reversed: Light, truth, the unravelling of involved matters, public rejoicings; according to another reading, vacillation.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.alt: A bearded ruler in armor and a red robe sits on a stone throne carved with rams' heads, holding an ankh scepter

reading.upright: Stability, power, protection, realization; a great person; aid, reason, conviction; also authority and will.
reading.reversed: Benevolence, compassion, credit; also confusion to enemies, obstruction, immaturity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.alt: A crowned priest raises his hand in blessing over two kneeling monks, crossed keys at his feet

reading.upright: Marriage, alliance, captivity, servitude; by another account, mercy and goodness; inspiration; the man to whom the Querent has recourse.
reading.reversed: Society, good understanding, concord, over-kindness, weakness.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot
notes: Printed 'over-' ends a line (p. 284) with 'kindness' on the next, so the scan cannot show whether the hyphen is part of the word. Kept 'over-kindness' as Wikisource's proofreaders read it; the sacred-texts transcription of the 1910 printing has 'overkindness'.

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.alt: A man and a woman stand beneath a winged angel, a fruit tree with a serpent behind her and a tree of flames behind him

reading.upright: Attraction, love, beauty, trials overcome.
reading.reversed: Failure, foolish designs. Another account speaks of marriage frustrated and contrarieties of all kinds.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.alt: A crowned charioteer stands in a canopied chariot drawn by a black sphinx and a white sphinx

reading.upright: Succour, providence; also war, triumph, presumption, vengeance, trouble.
reading.reversed: Riot, quarrel, dispute, litigation, defeat.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Strength
cards.alt: A woman in white gently closes the jaws of a lion, a figure eight floating above her head

reading.upright: Power, energy, action, courage, magnanimity; also complete success and honours.
reading.reversed: Despotism, abuse of power, weakness, discord, sometimes even disgrace.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot
notes: Waite heads this entry 'Fortitude'; the card is numbered 8 and is titled 'Strength' on the card and 'Strength, or Fortitude' in Part II. The site shows the card's own title, Strength; Waite's heading is kept in nameInWaite.

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.alt: A cloaked old man stands on a snowy peak holding up a lantern with a star inside

reading.upright: Prudence, circumspection; also and especially treason, dissimulation, roguery, corruption.
reading.reversed: Concealment, disguise, policy, fear, unreasoned caution.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.alt: A great wheel marked with letters turns in the sky, a sphinx on top, a serpent and a jackal-headed figure at its sides, winged creatures in the corners

reading.upright: Destiny, fortune, success, elevation, luck, felicity.
reading.reversed: Increase, abundance, superfluity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Justice
cards.alt: A crowned figure in red sits between two pillars holding an upright sword and a pair of scales

reading.upright: Equity, rightness, probity, executive; triumph of the deserving side in law.
reading.reversed: Law in all its departments, legal complications, bigotry, bias, excessive severity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.alt: A man hangs upside down by one foot from a living wooden cross, calm, a halo around his head

reading.upright: Wisdom, circumspection, discernment, trials, sacrifice, intuition, divination, prophecy.
reading.reversed: Selfishness, the crowd, body politic.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Death
cards.alt: A skeleton in black armor rides a white horse with a black banner marked by a white rose, people falling and kneeling before it

reading.upright: End, mortality, destruction, corruption; also, for a man, the loss of a benefactor; for a woman, many contrarieties; for a maid, failure of marriage projects.
reading.reversed: Inertia, sleep, lethargy, petrifaction, somnambulism; hope destroyed.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Temperance
cards.alt: A winged angel with one foot in a pool pours water between two cups, a path leading to a distant crown of light

reading.upright: Economy, moderation, frugality, management, accommodation.
reading.reversed: Things connected with churches, religions, sects, the priesthood, sometimes even the priest who will marry the Querent; also disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: The Devil
cards.alt: A horned, bat-winged figure crouches on a block above a chained man and woman who wear small horns and tails

reading.upright: Ravage, violence, vehemence, extraordinary efforts, force, fatality; that which is predestined but is not for this reason evil.
reading.reversed: Evil fatality, weakness, pettiness, blindness.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The Tower
cards.alt: Lightning strikes a tall tower and knocks off its crown as flames burst from the windows and two people fall

reading.upright: Misery, distress, indigence, adversity, calamity, disgrace, deception, ruin. It is a card in particular of unforeseen catastrophe.
reading.reversed: According to one account, the same in a lesser degree; also oppression, imprisonment, tyranny.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The Star
cards.alt: A naked woman kneels by a pool pouring water from two jugs onto the land and into the pool, a large star and seven small stars above

reading.upright: Loss, theft, privation, abandonment; another reading says—hope and bright prospects,
reading.reversed: Arrogance, haughtiness, impotence.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot
notes: Printed with a comma before 'Reversed' ('bright prospects, Reversed:'), where a full stop is expected. Kept as printed; the other source agrees.

cards.name: The Moon
cards.alt: A moon with a face shines over a path between two towers as a dog and a wolf howl and a crayfish climbs from a pool

reading.upright: Hidden enemies, danger, calumny, darkness, terror, deception, occult forces, error.
reading.reversed: Instability, inconstancy, silence, lesser degrees of deception and error.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: The Sun
cards.alt: A smiling sun shines on a child riding a white horse with a red banner, sunflowers along a wall behind

reading.upright: Material happiness, fortunate marriage, contentment.
reading.reversed: The same in a lesser sense.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Judgement
cards.alt: An angel blows a trumpet from the clouds as men, women, and children rise from their coffins with open arms

reading.upright: Change of position, renewal, outcome. Another account specifies total loss though lawsuit.
reading.reversed: Weakness, pusillanimity, simplicity; also deliberation, decision, sentence.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot
notes: Printed 'total loss though lawsuit', probably a misprint for 'through'. Kept as printed; the other source agrees.

cards.name: The World
cards.alt: A dancing figure wrapped in a sash holds two wands inside an oval wreath, an angel, an eagle, a bull, and a lion in the corners

reading.upright: Assured success, recompense, voyage, route, emigration, flight, change of place.
reading.reversed: Inertia, fixity, stagnation, permanence.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.alt: A hand reaches from a cloud holding a sprouting wand over a green valley with a castle

reading.upright: Creation, invention, enterprise, the powers which result in these; principle, beginning, source; birth, family, origin, and in a sense the virility which is behind them; the starting point of enterprises; according to another account, money, fortune, inheritance.
reading.reversed: Fall, decadence, ruin, perdition, to perish; also a certain clouded joy.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.alt: A man on a battlement holds a small globe and looks out over sea and land, one wand in his hand and another fixed to the wall

reading.upright: Between the alternative readings there is no marriage possible; on the one hand, riches, fortune, magnificence; on the other, physical suffering, disease, chagrin, sadness, mortification. The design gives one suggestion; here is a lord overlooking his dominion and alternately contemplating a globe; it looks like the malady, the mortification, the sadness of Alexander amidst the grandeur of this world’s wealth.
reading.reversed: Surprise, wonder, enchantment, emotion, trouble, fear.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.alt: A man stands on a cliff with his back to us watching ships at sea, three wands planted around him

reading.upright: He symbolizes established strength, enterprise, effort, trade, commerce, discovery; those are his ships, bearing his merchandise, which are sailing over the sea. The card also signifies able co-operation in business, as if the successful merchant prince were looking from his side towards yours with a view to help you.
reading.reversed: The end of troubles, suspension or cessation of adversity, toil and disappointment.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.alt: Four wands hung with a garland of flowers stand before a castle, two figures raising bouquets in welcome

reading.upright: They are for once almost on the surface—country life, haven of refuge, a species of domestic harvest-home, repose, concord, harmony, prosperity, peace, and the perfected work of these.
reading.reversed: The meaning remains unaltered; it is prosperity, increase, felicity, beauty, embellishment.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.alt: Five young men brandish wands at one another in a mock fight

reading.upright: Imitation, as, for example, sham fight, but also the strenuous competition and struggle of the search after riches and fortune. In this sense it connects with the battle of life. Hence some attributions say that it is a card of gold, gain, opulence.
reading.reversed: Litigation, disputes, trickery, contradiction.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.alt: A rider crowned with laurel carries a wreathed wand through a crowd holding wands

reading.upright: The card has been so designed that it can cover several significations; on the surface, it is a victor triumphing, but it is also great news, such as might be carried in state by the King’s courier; it is expectation crowned with its own desire, the crown of hope, and so forth.
reading.reversed: Apprehension, fear, as of a victorious enemy at the gate; treachery, disloyalty, as of gates being opened to the enemy; also indefinite delay.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.alt: A man on a hill defends himself with one wand against six wands rising from below

reading.upright: It is a card of valour, for, on the surface, six are attacking one, who has, however, the vantage position. On the intellectual plane, it signifies discussion, wordy strife; in business—negotiations, war of trade, barter, competition. It is further a card of success, for the combatant is on the top and his enemies may be unable to reach him.
reading.reversed: Perplexity, embarrassments, anxiety. It is also a caution against indecision.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.alt: Eight wands fly through the air in parallel over a river and open country

reading.upright: Activity in undertakings, the path of such activity, swiftness, as that of an express messenger; great haste, great hope, speed towards an end which promises assured felicity; generally, that which is on the move; also the arrows of love.
reading.reversed: Arrows of jealousy, internal dispute, stingings of conscience, quarrels; and domestic disputes for persons who are married.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.alt: A man with a bandaged head stands on guard with a wand, eight more wands behind him like a fence

reading.upright: The card signifies strength in opposition. If attacked, the person will meet an onslaught boldly; and his build shews that he may prove a formidable antagonist. With this main significance there are all its possible adjuncts—delay, suspension, adjournment.
reading.reversed: Obstacles, adversity, calamity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.alt: A man bends under the weight of ten wands as he carries them toward a town

reading.upright: A card of many significances, and some of the readings cannot be harmonized. I set aside that which connects it with honour and good faith. The chief meaning is oppression simply, but it is also fortune, gain, any kind of success, and then it is the oppression of these things. It is also a card of false-seeming, disguise, perfidy. The place which the figure is approaching may suffer from the rods that he carries. Success is stultified if the Nine of Swords follows, and if it is a question of a lawsuit, there will be certain loss.
reading.reversed: Contrarieties, difficulties, intrigues, and their analogies.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.alt: A young man in a patterned tunic stands in a desert holding a tall sprouting wand and looking up at its top

reading.upright: Dark young man, faithful, a lover, an envoy, a postman. Beside a man, he will bear favourable testimony concerning him. A dangerous rival, if followed by the Page of Cups. Has the chief qualities of his suit. He may signify family intelligence.
reading.reversed: Anecdotes, announcements, evil news. Also indecision and the instability which accompanies it.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.alt: A knight in armor on a rearing horse holds a sprouting wand, pyramids in the distance

reading.upright: Departure, absence, flight, emigration. A dark young man, friendly. Change of residence.
reading.reversed: Rupture, division, interruption, discord.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.alt: A crowned queen on a throne carved with lions holds a wand and a sunflower, a black cat at her feet

reading.upright: A dark woman, countrywoman, friendly, chaste, loving, honourable. If the card beside her signifies a man, she is well disposed towards him; if a woman, she is interested in the Querent. Also, love of money, or a certain success in business.
reading.reversed: Good, economical, obliging, serviceable. Signifies also—but in certain positions and in the neighbourhood of other cards tending in such directions—opposition, jealousy, even deceit and infidelity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.alt: A crowned king on a throne decorated with lions and salamanders holds a sprouting wand, a small salamander beside him

reading.upright: Dark man, friendly, countryman, generally married, honest and conscientious. The card always signifies honesty, and may mean news concerning an unexpected heritage to fall in before very long.
reading.reversed: Good, but severe; austere, yet tolerant.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.alt: A hand from a cloud holds a cup overflowing in five streams, a dove descending into it above a pool of water lilies

reading.upright: House of the true heart, joy, content, abode, nourishment, abundance, fertility; Holy Table, felicity hereof.
reading.reversed: House of the false heart, mutation, instability, revolution.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.alt: A young man and woman exchange cups, a winged lion's head above a staff with two serpents between them

reading.upright: Love, passion, friendship, affinity, union, concord, sympathy, the interrelation of the sexes, and—as a suggestion apart from all offices of divination—that desire which is not in Nature, but by which Nature is sanctified.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot
notes: No Reversed meaning is printed for this card (page 222); reversed is null. Source B also has none.
"interrelation": printed "inter-/relation" split at a line end, so the hyphen may be a real one ("inter-relation"); A and B both read "interrelation".

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.alt: Three women raise cups together in a harvest dance among fruit and flowers

reading.upright: The conclusion of any matter in plenty, perfection and merriment; happy issue, victory, fulfilment, solace, healing.
reading.reversed: Expedition, dispatch, achievement, end. It signifies also the side of excess in physical enjoyment, and the pleasures of the senses.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.alt: A young man sits under a tree with folded arms, three cups before him and a hand from a cloud offering a fourth

reading.upright: Weariness, disgust, aversion, imaginary vexations, as if the wine of this world had caused satiety only; another wine, as if a fairy gift, is now offered the wastrel, but he sees no consolation therein. This is also a card of blended pleasure.
reading.reversed: Novelty, presage, new instruction, new relations.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.alt: A cloaked figure mourns over three spilled cups, two full cups standing behind, a bridge leading to a house across a river

reading.upright: It is a card of loss, but something remains over; three have been taken, but two are left; it is a card of inheritance, patrimony, transmission, but not corresponding to expectations; with some interpreters it is a card of marriage, but not without bitterness or frustration.
reading.reversed: News, alliances, affinity, consanguinity, ancestry, return, false projects.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.alt: Two children in an old garden, one handing the other a cup of white flowers, more cups of flowers around them

reading.upright: A card of the past and of memories, looking back, as—for example—on childhood; happiness, enjoyment, but coming rather from the past; things that have vanished. Another reading reverses this, giving new relations, new knowledge, new environment, and then the children are disporting in an unfamiliar precinct.
reading.reversed: The future, renewal, that which will come to pass presently.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.alt: A figure faces seven cups floating in clouds, each holding a vision: a head, a veiled figure, a snake, a castle, jewels, a wreath, and a dragon

reading.upright: Fairy favours, images of reflection, sentiment, imagination, things seen in the glass of contemplation; some attainment in these degrees, but nothing permanent or substantial is suggested.
reading.reversed: Desire, will, determination, project.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.alt: A cloaked man with a staff walks away from eight stacked cups toward mountains under an eclipsed moon

reading.upright: The card speaks for itself on the surface, but other readings are entirely antithetical—giving joy, mildness, timidity, honour, modesty. In practice, it is usually found that the card shews the decline of a matter, or that a matter which has been thought to be important is really of slight consequence—either for good or evil.
reading.reversed: Great joy, happiness, feasting.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.alt: A contented man sits with arms folded before a curved table of nine cups

reading.upright: Concord, contentment, physical bien-être; also victory, success, advantage; satisfaction for the Querent or person for whom the consultation is made.
reading.reversed: Truth, loyalty, liberty; but the readings vary and include mistakes, imperfections, etc.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.alt: A couple with raised arms and two dancing children look up at a rainbow of ten cups above their home

reading.upright: Contentment, repose of the entire heart; the perfection of that state; also perfection of human love and friendship; if with several picture-cards, a person who is taking charge of the Querent’s interests; also the town, village or country inhabited by the Querent.
reading.reversed: Repose of the false heart, indignation, violence.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.alt: A young man in a flowered tunic stands by the sea looking at a fish rising from the cup in his hand

reading.upright: Fair young man, one impelled to render service and with whom the Querent will be connected; a studious youth; news, message; application, reflection, meditation; also these things directed to business.
reading.reversed: Taste, inclination, attachment, seduction, deception, artifice.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.alt: A knight in a winged helmet rides a calm white horse, holding a cup out before him

reading.upright: Arrival, approach—sometimes that of a messenger; advances, proposition, demeanour, invitation, incitement.
reading.reversed: Trickery, artifice, subtlety, swindling, duplicity, fraud.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.alt: A queen on a throne at the water's edge gazes at an ornate covered cup in her hands

reading.upright: Good, fair woman; honest, devoted woman, who will do service to the Querent; loving intelligence, and hence the gift of vision; success, happiness, pleasure; also wisdom, virtue; a perfect spouse and a good mother.
reading.reversed: The accounts vary; good woman; otherwise, distinguished woman but one not to be trusted; perverse woman; vice, dishonour, depravity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.alt: A king on a throne set on a rough sea holds a cup and a short scepter, a ship and a leaping fish behind him

reading.upright: Fair man, man of business, law, or divinity; responsible, disposed to oblige the Querent; also equity, art and science, including those who profess science, law and art; creative intelligence.
reading.reversed: Dishonest, double-dealing man; roguery, exaction, injustice, vice, scandal, pillage, considerable loss.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Ace of Swords
cards.alt: A hand from a cloud holds an upright sword crowned with a wreath above rocky peaks

reading.upright: Triumph, the excessive degree in everything, conquest, triumph of force. It is a card of great force, in love as well as in hatred. The crown may carry a much higher significance than comes usually within the sphere of fortune-telling.
reading.reversed: The same, but the results are disastrous; another account says—conception, childbirth, augmentation, multiplicity.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.alt: A blindfolded woman in white sits by the sea with two swords crossed over her chest

reading.upright: Conformity and the equipoise which it suggests, courage, friendship, concord in a state of arms; another reading gives tenderness, affection, intimacy. The suggestion of harmony and other favourable readings must be considered in a qualified manner, as Swords generally are not symbolical of beneficent forces in human affairs.
reading.reversed: Imposture, falsehood, duplicity, disloyalty.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.alt: Three swords pierce a red heart against grey clouds and rain

reading.upright: Removal, absence, delay, division, rupture, dispersion, and all that the design signifies naturally, being too simple and obvious to call for specific enumeration.
reading.reversed: Mental alienation, error, loss, distraction, disorder, confusion.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.alt: A knight lies in effigy on a tomb in a church, hands joined in prayer, three swords on the wall and one along the tomb

reading.upright: Vigilance, retreat, solitude, hermit’s repose, exile, tomb and coffin. It is these last that have suggested the design.
reading.reversed: Wise administration, circumspection, economy, avarice, precaution, testament.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Five of Swords
cards.alt: A man gathers swords with a sly look as two defeated figures walk away toward the sea

reading.upright: Degradation, destruction, revocation, infamy, dishonour, loss, with the variants and analogues of these.
reading.reversed: The same; burial and obsequies.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Six of Swords
cards.alt: A ferryman poles a boat carrying a cloaked woman and a child across water, six swords standing upright in the boat

reading.upright: Journey by water, route, way, envoy, commissionary, expedient.
reading.reversed: Declaration, confession, publicity; one account says that it is a proposal of love.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Seven of Swords
cards.alt: A man tiptoes away from a camp carrying five swords, two left standing behind him

reading.upright: Design, attempt, wish, hope, confidence; also quarrelling, a plan that may fail, annoyance. The design is uncertain in its import, because the significations are widely at variance with each other.
reading.reversed: Good advice, counsel, instruction, slander, babbling.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Eight of Swords
cards.alt: A blindfolded woman in red stands bound among eight swords planted in wet ground, a castle on a hill behind

reading.upright: Bad news, violent chagrin, crisis, censure, power in trammels, conflict, calumny; also sickness.
reading.reversed: Disquiet, difficulty, opposition, accident, treachery; what is unforeseen; fatality.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Nine of Swords
cards.alt: A woman sits up in bed with her face in her hands, nine swords hanging on the dark wall behind her

reading.upright: Death, failure, miscarriage, delay, deception, disappointment, despair.
reading.reversed: Imprisonment, suspicion, doubt, reasonable fear, shame.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Ten of Swords
cards.alt: A man lies face down under a dark sky with ten swords in his back, a pale dawn along the horizon

reading.upright: Whatsoever is intimated by the design; also pain, affliction, tears, sadness, desolation. It is not especially a card of violent death.
reading.reversed: Advantage, profit, success, favour, but none of these are permanent; also power and authority.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

transcription.from: Wikisource (proofread and validated), checked against the Internet Archive text a.-e.-waite-the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot

cards.name: Page of Swords
cards.alt: A young man on rough ground holds a sword upright in both hands, clouds and birds in the sky

reading.upright: Authority, overseeing, secret service, vigilance, spying, examination, and the qualities thereto belonging.
reading.reversed: More evil side of these qualities; what is unforeseen, unprepared state; sickness is also intimated.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Knight of Swords
cards.alt: A knight in armor charges on a galloping horse, sword raised, trees bending in the wind

reading.upright: Skill, bravery, capacity, defence, address, enmity, wrath, war, destruction, opposition, resistance, ruin. There is therefore a sense in which the card signifies death, but it carries this meaning only in its proximity to other cards of fatality.
reading.reversed: Imprudence, incapacity, extravagance.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Queen of Swords
cards.alt: A crowned queen on a throne among clouds holds an upright sword and lifts her other hand

reading.upright: Widowhood, female sadness and embarrassment, absence, sterility, mourning, privation, separation.
reading.reversed: Malice, bigotry, artifice, prudery, bale, deceit.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: King of Swords
cards.alt: A king on a throne carved with butterflies faces us, holding an upright sword

reading.upright: Whatsoever arises out of the idea of judgment and all its connexions—power, command, authority, militant intelligence, law, offices of the crown, and so forth.
reading.reversed: Cruelty, perversity, barbarity, perfidy, evil intention.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.alt: A hand from a cloud holds a large golden pentacle over a garden with an arch of white roses

reading.upright: Perfect contentment, felicity, ecstasy; also speedy intelligence; gold.
reading.reversed: The evil side of wealth, bad intelligence; also great riches. In any case it shews prosperity, comfortable material conditions, but whether these are of advantage to the possessor will depend on whether the card is reversed or not.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.alt: A young man dances while juggling two pentacles in a loop, ships riding high waves behind him

reading.upright: On the one hand it is represented as a card of gaiety, recreation and its connexions, which is the subject of the design; but it is read also as news and messages in writing, as obstacles, agitation, trouble, embroilment.
reading.reversed: Enforced gaiety, simulated enjoyment, literal sense, handwriting, composition, letters of exchange.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.alt: A stonemason on a bench works in a church arch while a monk and a hooded figure hold plans, three pentacles carved above

reading.upright: Métier, trade, skilled labour; usually, however, regarded as a card of nobility, aristocracy, renown, glory.
reading.reversed: Mediocrity, in work and otherwise, puerility, pettiness, weakness.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.alt: A crowned man clutches a pentacle to his chest, one on his crown and two under his feet, a city behind

reading.upright: The surety of possessions, cleaving to that which one has, gift, legacy, inheritance.
reading.reversed: Suspense, delay, opposition.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.alt: Two poor figures, one on crutches, walk through snow past a lit church window with five pentacles

reading.upright: The card foretells material trouble above all, whether in the form illustrated—that is, destitution—or otherwise. For some cartomancists, it is a card of love and lovers—wife, husband, friend, mistress; also concordance, affinities. These alternatives cannot be harmonized.
reading.reversed: Disorder, chaos, ruin, discord, profligacy.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.alt: A merchant weighs coins in a pair of scales and gives alms to two kneeling beggars

reading.upright: Presents, gifts, gratification; another account says attention, vigilance; now is the accepted time, present prosperity, etc.
reading.reversed: Desire, cupidity, envy, jealousy, illusion.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.alt: A young farmer leans on his hoe and looks at seven pentacles growing on a green bush

reading.upright: These are exceedingly contradictory; in the main, it is a card of money, business, barter; but one reading gives altercation, quarrel—and another innocence, ingenuity, purgation.
reading.reversed: Cause for anxiety regarding money which it may be proposed to lend.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

cards.alt: A craftsman at a bench carves a pentacle, finished pentacles hung beside him

reading.upright: Work, employment, commission, craftsmanship, skill in craft and business, perhaps in the preparatory stage.
reading.reversed: Voided ambition, vanity, cupidity, exaction, usury. It may also signify the possession of skill, in the sense of the ingenious mind turned to cunning and intrigue.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

reading.upright: Prudence, safety, success, accomplishment, certitude, discernment.
reading.reversed: Roguery, deception, voided project, bad faith.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

reading.upright: Gain, riches; family matters, archives, extraction, the abode of a family.
reading.reversed: Chance, fatality, loss, robbery, games of hazard; sometimes gift, dowry, pension.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

reading.upright: Application, study, scholarship, reflection; another reading says news, messages and the bringer thereof; also rule, management.
reading.reversed: Prodigality, dissipation, liberality. luxury; unfavourable news.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

reading.upright: Utility, serviceableness, interest, responsibility, rectitude—all on the normal and external plane.

reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

reading.reversed: Evil, suspicion, suspense, fear, mistrust.
reading.credit: From A. E. Waite's 1911 Pictorial Key to the Tarot.

reading.upright: Valour, realizing intelligence, business and normal intellectual aptitude, sometimes mathematical gifts and attainments of this kind; success in these paths.
